thesis: Held. Linde's Oct 29 Q3 2026 report showed record sales of $9.4B (+9%) and adjusted EPS of $4.59 (+9%), and management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $17.82-$17.92. This suggests the core industrial-gas pricing/productivity model is intact and still supports holding, even though reported EPS fell 11% on a $425M cost-reduction charge (a one-off restructuring item rather than an operating deterioration). Q4 guidance ($4.40-$4.50) assumes no economic improvement, so upside from here relies on execution rather than macro; the stock sits ~6.6% below its 52-week high after a +12.6% 60-day move. No new litigation or governance items surfaced.
invalidation: Q4 adjusted EPS below the $4.40-$4.50 guide or another cut to full-year guidance; further charges signaling the restructuring is broader than disclosed

thesis: Home Depot reported Q3 fiscal 2026 on Nov 17: sales $43.4B (+4.9%), comparable sales +2.2% (vs a Zacks model of +0.8%), and adjusted EPS $3.86 vs $3.74, and it updated FY26 guidance (adjusted EPS ~+2%). That confirmed beat on comps suggests the home-improvement demand trough is easing and sits behind the +14% 60-day move. The counter-case is that full-year EPS growth guidance is only ~2% and housing turnover remains weak, and I couldn't verify the updated comp guide from the primary release. The stock eased ~0.4% after the print, so the read is positive but not decisive.
invalidation: Q4 comps turning negative or another cut to FY26 EPS guidance

thesis: Held. Costco's company-reported October 2026 sales (four weeks ended Nov 1) rose 12.6% to $24.50B, following +13% in September and +9.9% in August, a confirmed, company-disclosed demand trend that drove a +23.6% 60-day move and a 52-week high on Nov 17. The strongest counter-evidence is valuation (P/E ~53; Zacks Hold notes fundamentals look priced in), but valuation alone isn't a deterioration in the business and doesn't change the read while comps are accelerating rather than slowing. Next binary event (Q1 FY27 earnings, mid-December) falls after the next review. No litigation or governance items surfaced.
invalidation: November monthly sales growth decelerating sharply (below high single digits) or a Q1 FY27 membership/renewal-rate miss

thesis: P&G is +17.6% over 60 days and ~1.9% below a 52-week high set Nov 17, after late-October fiscal Q1 results beat estimates (EPS $2.00 vs $1.89) and the company raised its sales/profit outlook. That is a confirmed company-disclosed catalyst suggesting staples volume/pricing momentum. However, P&G's Investor Day is tomorrow (Nov 19, 2pm ET), a pending event before the next review that could reset multi-year targets either way, and executives have flagged rising promotional volumes. So this stays medium. No litigation or governance items surfaced.
invalidation: Investor Day targets below consensus, or evidence that higher promotion is eroding margins

thesis: Held. Lilly's Q3 2026 8-K showed revenue of $24.4B (+39%), Zepbound ~+49%, and a full-year revenue guide raised to $91-$92B from $85-$87B, a confirmed company-disclosed catalyst behind the +21.5% 60-day move and a 52-week high on Nov 16. The strongest counter-evidence is management's own note that some 2026 revenue was one-time, plus a pending Strive compounding-pharmacy antitrust suit; even with those, the incretin franchise growth (63% US GLP-1 share) is large enough that one-time items don't change the read, and the Strive suit has no scheduled ruling found in the next ~90 days. Next earnings are February 2027.
invalidation: Material FDA action restricting Foundayo/Zepbound, guidance cut, or a court ruling in the compounding antitrust case adverse to Lilly

thesis: Held. Visa is +12.7% over 60 days and ~6% below its Nov 5 52-week high, but this run's search surfaced no specific new company-disclosed catalyst for November; the only material item found is the long-running DOJ debit-monopolization suit (SDNY), which has no scheduled ruling or trial date surfaced in the next ~90 days. With no identified catalyst the move reads as momentum/sentiment rather than a disclosed fundamental change, so the evidence still supports holding but only weakly.
invalidation: An adverse ruling or remedy in the DOJ debit case, or a payments-volume slowdown in the next quarterly report

thesis: SK hynix ADRs are down ~35% over 60 days amid a memory-sector selloff (Nov 5-6 drops of ~9-10% in Seoul tied to post-midterm AI-regulation fears, then falling NAND prices); the ADR is ~39% below its 52-week high and near its 52-week low. On Nov 17 a US judge refused to dismiss a DRAM price-fixing class action against SK hynix, Samsung and Micron (no scheduled ruling found). The catalyst is sector-wide rather than company-specific, and Samsung Securities' view that the price already discounts a ~36% memory-price fall conflicts with Counterpoint saying prices are still rising, so there is no clear long read. Trend filter skipped (only 92 daily bars since the July 2026 ADR listing).
invalidation: Stabilizing DRAM/HBM contract prices plus a recovery in the memory complex

thesis: Held. Apple reported record September-quarter revenue of $114.5B (+12%) and made its first-ever close above $350 on Nov 9, now ~2.4% below its 52-week high. The confirmed earnings result suggests demand is supporting the valuation. Counter-evidence: the DOJ antitrust case (discovery phase, trial likely 2027) and undated reports of settlement talks; no ruling is scheduled within ~90 days, but the settlement-talk terms are unknown and not engaged with enough to dismiss, so this stays below high.
invalidation: DOJ settlement terms or ruling that materially restrict App Store/services economics, or a guide-down on the December-quarter outlook

thesis: AMD is down ~18% over 60 days, largely from a sector-wide semiconductor selloff (-17.3% on Nov 5 on post-midterm AI-regulation fears, and a two-day ~13% slide before Nvidia's report). It rebounded today (+5.4%) after Nvidia's blowout quarter, and it remains above its 200-day average. Company-specific items are supportive (Taalas acquisition finalized; management talking up 2027 revenue growth >80%), but the drivers of the 60-day move are macro/sector-wide rather than company-disclosed. That suggests a long bias only at low conviction.
invalidation: Renewed semiconductor selloff taking AMD below its 200-day average, or concrete US AI data-center restrictions

thesis: AES is subject to a $15.00/share cash take-private by a GIP/EQT-led consortium; FERC issued the final suspensory regulatory approval on Nov 17, 2026 and closing is expected Dec 2, 2026, after which the stock delists. Today's 10.9x volume spike is consistent with merger-arbitrage repositioning after that approval. With the price at $15.01 (at/above the cash consideration) there is no upside left for a new entry, only deal-break downside. Closing is still pending, and shareholder suits over deal price remain, so this is not rated high.

BIPC's 5.5x volume spike and +11% 60-day move coincide with Brookfield Infrastructure's corporate simplification, which closes Nov 19, 2026: BIPC holders automatically receive Brookfield Infrastructure Partners Inc. Class A shares 1:1, trading as 'BIP' from about Nov 23. The volume looks largely mechanical (index/holder repositioning ahead of the conversion) rather than a fundamental change, even though Q3 FFO/unit rose ~10% to $0.91. With the BIPC symbol about to stop trading and no Q4 distribution declared, a new entry in this ticker isn't sensible.
invalidation: Simplification delayed or cancelled (BIPC continues trading as a standalone security)

thesis: Global-e reported Q3 2026 results on Nov 18: GMV ~$2.04B (+35%, near the top of its $1.995-$2.045B guide), revenue $314M (+42%), and a raised full-year GMV outlook to $8.957-$9.117B. This is a confirmed company-disclosed catalyst and suggests continued share gains in cross-border e-commerce. The counter-evidence is the market's own reaction: the stock fell ~4.5% on 5.2x volume, suggesting the raise fell short of elevated expectations (previews called the bar high), and sources disagree on Q4 adjusted EBITDA guidance. That reaction isn't resolved by the numbers, so this stays medium. No litigation, dilution, or governance items surfaced.
invalidation: Q4 GMV tracking below the $3.085B low end of guidance, or a merchant-concentration/Shopify partnership change

thesis: Primo Brands fell ~6% today on 4.6x volume with no company announcement identified (Finviz: no clear catalyst), giving back part of a +18% 60-day move; Deutsche Bank recently cut its target to $21 (Hold) in a Q3 preview. The company still carries two securities class actions (D. Conn. and M.D. Fla.) over the botched BlueTriton integration and the November 2025 guidance cut and CEO change, with no scheduled ruling found within ~90 days. The move reads as sentiment-driven rather than a disclosed fundamental change, and the integration overhang suggests no clear long setup.
invalidation: A disclosed fundamental catalyst (e.g., guidance raise or integration milestones) that reverses the selling
